text:
maria: FYI I'm trying to add a new GPU node pool (nvidia A100) via Terraform in us-west1. Terraform apply succeeds, nodes show up in the cluster, but cluster-autoscaler never scales up for pending GPU pods. Anyone seen this?

cheng: Did you set taints on the node pool? CA won't consider nodes if pods can't schedule on them.

maria: Yes, we added a taint "gpu=true:NoSchedule" and pods have tolerations + nodeSelector for the accelerator. We're on GKE Standard. CA logs show 'ScaleUp: no suitable nodes found' and then 'No unschedulable pods' — weird. Here's the Terraform snippet for the node pool we used:

```hcl
module "gpu_pool" {
  source = "terraform-google-modules/kubernetes-engine/google//modules/node_pool"
  name   = "np-gpu-a100-usw1"
  node_count = 0
  node_config = {
    machine_type = "n1-standard-16"
    accelerators = [{ type = "nvidia-tesla-a100", count = 1 }]
    taint = ["gpu:NoSchedule"] # <- suspect formatting issue?
  }
  autoscaling = { min_node_count = 0, max_node_count = 10 }
}
```

sam: Two things to check: 1) CA discovers node groups by GCE instance group labels for GKE, so make sure the CA Helm chart is installed with node-group discovery for GKE, and 2) formatting of the taint matters — CA and Kube scheduler expect the key=value:effect form for matching tolerations.

cheng: Also check whether you have a mutating webhook that injects tolerations later (eg. a sidecar injector or pod mutator). If the toleration is added after admission or by a later mutation, CA might see the pod as unschedulable differently.

julian: FWIW I hit this before — terraform often ends up creating the taint without the `=value` part if code was copied from older examples. In our case TF created `gpu:NoSchedule` not `gpu=true:NoSchedule`. CA/scheduler compare toleration keys exactly. Example correct TF field:

```hcl
node_config {
  taint = ["gpu=true:NoSchedule"]
}
```

maria: OMG that was it — my copy/paste removed the `=true`. I changed taint to `gpu=true:NoSchedule` and re-applied. CA scaled up within ~45s and pods started scheduling. :tada:

leo: For the infra chart we should make CA explicit in Helm values. Suggested flags for cluster-autoscaler in our Helm values: `--expander=least-waste`, `--balance-similar-node-groups`, and ensure discovery flags for GKE are set. Also ensure we don't accidentally pass `--skip-nodes-with-system-pods` in a way that hides GPU pools. Example values snippet:

```yaml
clusterAutoscaler:
  enabled: true
  extraArgs:
    expander: "least-waste"
    balance-similar-node-groups: "true"
    skip-nodes-with-local-storage: "false"
  nodeGroupDiscovery:
    gke: true
```

ops-bot: terraform plan shows change: module.gke.node_pool["np-gpu-a100-usw1"].node_config.taint will be updated from ["gpu:NoSchedule"] to ["gpu=true:NoSchedule"]. No other changes. :white_check_mark:

sam: Let's add an e2e test to CI: create a pod with the GPU toleration and nodeSelector and assert CA scales the pool up within 2 minutes. I'll open a ticket and a small test harness.

maria: I'll open a PR to fix the TF module default and also add a note in the Helm values defaults so this doesn't regress. Thanks everybody :heart:
